# seny

**Sanity checks for differential gene Expression in NoisY data** (and
*seny*, the Catalan word for common sense).

For every cluster-by-contrast comparison in a multi-sample single-cell
dataset, `seny` decides whether a pseudobulk differential-expression
test is **Adequate**, **Underpowered**, **Caution** or **Invalid**, and
explains why. The diagnostics are analytic and run on your own data —
there is no per-dataset simulation.

| Call | Meaning |
|----|----|
| **Invalid** | Type I error cannot be trusted (design not estimable, too few samples per group). |
| **Caution** | Valid, but a risk applies (condition confounded with a covariate, or cell-count imbalance tracking the condition). |
| **Underpowered** | Valid but unable to detect the target effect (sensitivity too low, or too few testable genes). |
| **Adequate** | No flags. |

The call has a severity order — Invalid \> Caution \> Underpowered \>
Adequate — and a `reason` string that lists every flag, so a single
headline never hides a second problem.

## Installation

`seny` is not yet on Bioconductor. Install the development version from
GitHub:

``` r

# install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("smorabit/seny")
```

## Usage

``` r

library(seny)

sce <- readRDS(system.file("extdata", "example_sce.rds", package = "seny"))

res <- assessAll(sce, sample = "donor", group = "condition",
                 annotations = "cell_type", targetLFC = 1)
res                         # one row per comparison: metrics, call, reason

plots <- plotAdequacy(res)  # traffic-light matrix, one ggplot per annotation set
plots[["cell_type"]]
```

See
[`vignette("seny")`](https://smorabit.github.io/seny/articles/seny.md)
for the full walk-through.

## Status

Experimental (P1 MVP). The package covers diagnostic layers 1, 2 and 4;
the call thresholds in
[`defaultThresholds()`](https://smorabit.github.io/seny/reference/defaultThresholds.md)
are **provisional placeholders** being recalibrated from a validation
study (OneK1K, AIDA and an in-house atlas). Outlier detection, empirical
checks, composition assessment, calibrated power and an HTML report are
planned.

# Package index

## Entry point

Run the whole assessment, or build the pseudobulk object the layers
share.

- [`assessAll()`](https://smorabit.github.io/seny/reference/assessAll.md)
  : Assess every pseudobulk comparison end to end
- [`pbSetup()`](https://smorabit.github.io/seny/reference/pbSetup.md) :
  Set up pseudobulk comparisons from a single-cell dataset

## Diagnostic layers

The per-comparison diagnostics, in order.

- [`assessDesign()`](https://smorabit.github.io/seny/reference/assessDesign.md)
  : Layer 1: design validity and confounding
- [`assessPseudobulk()`](https://smorabit.github.io/seny/reference/assessPseudobulk.md)
  : Layer 2: pseudobulk quality
- [`estimateVariance()`](https://smorabit.github.io/seny/reference/estimateVariance.md)
  : Layer 4 (variance): null-model dispersion, decomposition and
  per-gene SE
- [`estimateSensitivity()`](https://smorabit.github.io/seny/reference/estimateSensitivity.md)
  : Layer 4 (sensitivity): minimum detectable effect and power

## Calling and reporting

Assemble the comparison table, make the call, and show the matrix.

- [`callComparisons()`](https://smorabit.github.io/seny/reference/callComparisons.md)
  : Assemble the comparison table and make the adequacy call
- [`defaultThresholds()`](https://smorabit.github.io/seny/reference/defaultThresholds.md)
  : Default decision thresholds for the adequacy call
- [`plotAdequacy()`](https://smorabit.github.io/seny/reference/plotAdequacy.md)
  : Traffic-light matrix of adequacy calls
